mechanism_narrative: The sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a continuing recovery in consumer activity, leading to further increases in retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility, exceeding a 10-point increase week-on-week (t-2w to t-1w), signals a return to office-based work which directly drives increased demand for retail and recreation services during weekdays, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES rising by more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and an increase in TRANSIT mobility indicates a shift away from home-bound activities and towards external engagement, suggesting a higher propensity for retail and recreation outings over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falling and TRANSIT rising concurrently for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks despite concurrent decreases in RESIDENTIAL and increases in TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM mobility around baseline for two consecutive weeks suggests that essential activity levels have normalized, implying that any further relaxation of restrictions or increase in confidence will primarily translate into non-essential RETAIL_REC activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within +/- 1 point of baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable near baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A recent decline in PARKS mobility for two consecutive weeks, following an earlier peak, combined with a concurrent rise in RETAIL_REC, suggests a substitution effect where people are shifting from outdoor recreational activities to indoor retail and entertainment, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC up over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility declines for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC increases
regime_hint: seasonal shift or post-lockdown activity rebalancing
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains flat over the next two weeks despite PARKS mobility declining and RETAIL_REC increasing in the preceding period.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past three weeks indicates a sustained reduction in time spent at home, freeing up more time for out-of-home activities including retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in TRANSIT mobility, with a week-on-week rise of at least 4 points for two consecutive weeks, signifies a broader return to public transportation for commuting and leisure, which will directly boost RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 4 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next week despite TRANSIT mobility rising by at least 4 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If the recent strong increase in WORKPLACES mobility stalls or reverses, while RESIDENTIAL mobility begins to rise again, it would indicate a reversal of the return-to-office trend and a shift back to home-based activities, leading to a decline in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by more than 5 points week-on-week AND RESIDENTIAL rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
regime_hint: re-tightening restrictions or new public health concerns
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases or remains stable over the next four weeks despite WORKPLACES falling and RESIDENTIAL rising as specified.
